paragraphs: Here's the big idea, baker: Psalm 1 says the blessed life is a rooted life. It opens with a man who won't walk, stand or sit with the wicked, but that's only half of it. The other half is the BUT: "his delight is in the Law of the LORD, and on His law he meditates day and night" (Psalm 1:2). He isn't just avoiding the wrong things. He's feeding on the right one.

Think about a tree planted by streams of water. It doesn't strain to make fruit or panic about the season. It just stays near the water, and the fruit comes "in season" (Psalm 1:3). Staying close to God's Word works the same way, friend. You don't have to be perfect in one big burst. You keep coming back to the stream, and that's how a life gets steady and fruitful.

Then the psalm gives the other side, and it's serious: the wicked are "like chaff driven off by the wind" (Psalm 1:4). No roots, nothing to hold them. But look at the last line: "the LORD guards the path of the righteous" (Psalm 1:6). So here's why this matters to you: the Word isn't aheavy rule you carry. It's the place where you get planted, and the LORD watches over the path you walk.
